name: ANTARES
full_name: Astronomy with a Neutrino Telescope and Abyss environmental RESearch
summary: Historical deep-sea neutrino telescope that searched for dark matter in the Sun and Galaxy; now shut down and dismantled.
detection_principle: Photomultiplier tubes record Cherenkov light from charged secondary particles produced by neutrinos in seawater, reconstructing upward-going tracks and cascades.

sites.name: Mediterranean Sea near Toulon, about 40 km from La Seyne-sur-Mer
sites.location: Mediterranean Sea near Toulon, about 40 km from La Seyne-sur-Mer

status.label: Data taking ended / historical experiment
status.evidence: Data taking stopped on 2022-02-12; the main detector was dismantled in May–June.

timeline.event: Recovery of the main seabed detector completed

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
